note: The thirteen law areas, derived from NCBE's public subject lists: the union of the MBE's, the MEE's (current and earlier) and the NextGen UBE's subjects, plus professional responsibility (the MPRE, and the Model Rules NextGen assesses from recall). NCBE's compound subjects stay one area each. Each outline is NCBE's top-level categories, verbatim, prefixed with the sub-subject where NCBE splits one; each assumption is NCBE's own governing-law note or question weight. Format codes carry no dates: SPEC-V2-2214 section 4.1 holds the dated facts. The DeckStreak architect maps private decks onto these ids in private configuration.

formats.mbe: Multistate Bar Examination: 175 scored multiple-choice questions, 25 per subject
formats.mee: Multistate Essay Examination, its current subject list: six essay questions
formats.mee-legacy: Multistate Essay Examination, its earlier subject list only
formats.mpt: Multistate Performance Test: tested with the legal resources provided
formats.nextgen: NextGen UBE foundational concepts and principles
formats.nextgen-resources: NextGen UBE skills questions, with the legal resources provided
formats.nextgen-integrated: NextGen UBE integrated question sets, from recall

areas.name: Business Associations

ncbe_names.mee: Business Associations (Agency and Partnership; Corporations and Limited Liability Companies)

outline: Agency and partnership: Power of agent to bind principal
Agency and partnership: Vicarious liability of principal for acts of agent
Agency and partnership: Fiduciary duties between principal and agent
Agency and partnership: Creation of partnerships
Agency and partnership: Power and liability of partners
Agency and partnership: Rights of partners among themselves
Agency and partnership: Special rules concerning limited partnerships
Corporations and limited liability companies: Formation of organizations
Corporations and limited liability companies: Pre-organization transactions
Corporations and limited liability companies: Piercing the veil
Corporations and limited liability companies: Financing the organization
Corporations and limited liability companies: Management and control
Corporations and limited liability companies: Fiduciary duties
Corporations and limited liability companies: Close corporations and special control devices
Corporations and limited liability companies: Organizational structure including relationships between parents and subsidiaries
Corporations and limited liability companies: Shareholder and member litigation: direct, derivative, and class litigation
assumptions: Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Civil Procedure
assumptions: Assume the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure as currently in effect, and the sections of Title 28 of the U.S. Code on trial and appellate jurisdiction, venue, and transfer.
On the MBE, about two-thirds of the questions come from categories I, III and V, and about one-third from the rest.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Conflict of Laws
outline: Recognition and enforcement of other states' judgments and foreign judgments
assumptions: Conflict of laws issues are embedded in the other MEE areas and do not appear as stand-alone questions.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Constitutional Law
outline: The relation of nation and states in a federal system
assumptions: The Constitution, constitutional and unconstitutional refer to the federal Constitution unless indicated otherwise.
On the MBE, about half of the questions come from category IV, individual rights.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Contracts

ncbe_names.mee: Contracts (including Article 2 [Sales] of the Uniform Commercial Code)

assumptions: Assume the Official Text of Articles 1 and 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code has been adopted and is in effect.
On the MBE, about half of the questions come from categories I and IV, and about one-fourth rest on Articles 1 and 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Criminal Law and Procedure

ncbe_names.nextgen: Criminal Law and Constitutional Protections of Accused Persons

assumptions: On the MBE, about half of the questions come from category V, constitutional protection of accused persons, and about half from categories I to IV.
On NextGen, the elements of crimes and defenses are tested on the basis of provided statutes.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Evidence
outline: Relevancy and reasons for excluding relevant evidence
Hearsay and circumstances of its admissibility
assumptions: Answer under the Federal Rules of Evidence as currently in effect.
On the MBE, about one-quarter of the questions come from category I, one-third from category II, one-quarter from category V, and the rest from categories III and IV.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Family Law
assumptions: On the MPT and in NextGen skills questions, family law is tested with the legal resources provided.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Professional Responsibility

ncbe_names.nextgen-integrated: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct, within the client counseling, negotiation and client relationship skills

outline: Competence, legal malpractice, and other civil liability
Litigation and other forms of advocacy
Transactions and communications with persons other than clients
Lawyers' duties to the public and the legal system
assumptions: The MPRE rests on the law governing the conduct and discipline of lawyers and judges: the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct, the ABA Model Code of Judicial Conduct, controlling constitutional decisions, and generally accepted principles from leading federal and state cases and procedural and evidentiary rules.
NextGen assesses, from recall and without the comments, ABA Model Rules 1.0, 1.1, 1.2(a) and (d), 1.3, 1.4, 1.6(a) and (c), 1.7, 3.1, 3.3(a)(1) and (2), 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3.
On the MPRE, conflicts of interest carry the largest share of questions, 12 to 18 percent.

areas.name: Real Property
assumptions: On the MBE, about one-fifth of the questions come from each of categories I to V.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Secured Transactions

ncbe_names.mee-legacy: Secured Transactions (Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code)

outline: Validity of security agreements and rights of parties
Rights of third parties; perfected and unperfected security interests; rules of priority
assumptions: Assume the Official Texts of Articles 1 and 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code have been adopted and are in effect.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Torts
assumptions: Assume that survival actions and claims for wrongful death are available.
Joint and several liability and pure comparative fault apply unless otherwise indicated.
On the MBE, about half of the questions come from category II, negligence.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.

areas.name: Trusts and Estates

ncbe_names.mee-legacy: Trusts and Estates (Decedents' Estates; Trusts and Future Interests)

outline: Decedents' estates: Living wills and durable health care powers
Trusts and future interests: Future interests
Trusts and future interests: Construction problems
assumptions: On the MPT and in NextGen skills questions, trusts and estates are tested with the legal resources provided.
Answer by generally accepted fundamental legal principles, as the MEE instructs.
